title: Graph problem solving: DSU, Dijkstra path, grid BFS
overview: A problem-solving module that applies earlier graph tools to judge problems. DSU tracks components while roads are added, and helps rebuild a road network. Dijkstra is extended to print the actual path, and BFS on a grid finds the fewest moves. The main skill is spotting which tool a story is really asking for.

concepts.explain: Start with `cmp = n`. Each union of two different groups does `cmp--`, and the new group's size can update the largest size.
An edge inside one component is useless; a pair of different components needs a link. Swap one for the other.
Whenever Dijkstra improves `dis[child]`, remember `par[child] = node`. At the end, walk `par` back from the target and reverse.
concepts.snippet:
for (v = n; v != -1; v = par[v]) path.push_back(v);
reverse(path.begin(), path.end());

concepts.explain: On a grid where every move costs 1, BFS reaches cells in order of distance, so `level[cell]` is the minimum number of moves.
Store the 4 moves as pairs and loop over them, checking bounds with a `valid` helper.
`while (cin >> n)` keeps processing test cases until input runs out.

files.title: CSES 1676: Road Construction
files.what: After each new road, print the number of components and the size of the largest one. DSU with union by size keeps both numbers up to date.
steps: If both ends already share a leader, nothing changes (early `return`).
Otherwise attach the smaller group, add the sizes, update `max_size` with the new size, and do `cmp--`.
files.complexity: Time about O(n + m) · Space O(n)
files.input_note: n m, then m roads. The first three roads are the CSES example; the fourth joins everything.
files.output_note: Lines `4 2`, `3 3`, `2 3`, `1 5`. After road 3-5 the groups {1,2,3} and {4,5} merge, so there is 1 component of size 5.

check.q: Why can `max_size` only grow, never shrink?
check.a: Roads are only added, so groups only merge. A merged group is at least as big as each part.

files.title: Codeforces 25D: Roads not only in Berland

problem.name: Codeforces 25D - Roads not only in Berland

files.what: There are n-1 roads. Every road that closes a cycle is wasted, and each wasted road can be moved to connect two components. Close the wasted roads and link every component to city 1.
steps: Read the n-1 roads. If a road's ends already share a leader, save it in `remove_roads`; otherwise union them.
Then for `i = 2..n`: if `find(i)` differs from `find(1)`, save `{1, i}` in `add_roads` and union them.
The number of wasted roads always equals the number of links needed, because n-1 roads and a tree needs n-1 edges.
Print the count, then pair the i-th removed road with the i-th new road on each line.
files.input_note: n, then n-1 roads. Road 3-1 closes the triangle 1-2-3, and {4,5,6,7} is cut off.
files.output_note: Prints `1` and `3 1 1 4`: close road 3-1 and build road 1-4. After that the whole country is connected.

check.a: With k components the forest uses n-k roads, so (n-1)-(n-k) = k-1 roads are wasted, and exactly k-1 links are needed to join k components.

files.title: Codeforces 20C: Dijkstra? (print the path)
files.what: Run Dijkstra from node 1 on an undirected weighted graph, remember each node's parent, and print the shortest path from 1 to n (or -1).
steps: Store edges both ways in `adj_list`; set `dis[i] = LLONG_MAX` and `par[i] = -1`.
Pop the closest node; for each neighbour, if the distance improves, update `dis`, push it, and set `par[child] = node`.
Otherwise follow `par` from n back to 1, reverse the list, and print it.
files.complexity: Time O((n + m) log n) · Space O(n + m)
files.input_note: n m, then m edges `a b w`. This is the Codeforces example (expected `1 4 3 5`).
files.output_note: The file does not compile, so no output appears. After the fix it prints `1 4 3 5` (cost 1+3+1 = 5, cheaper than 1-2-5 = 7).
files.watch_out: Inside `dijkstra` the popped pair is named `par`, which hides the global array `par[]`, so `par[child_node] = par_node` fails to compile. Rename the local variable (for example `pair<ll,ll> cur = pq.top();`). Also add `#include <climits>` for `LLONG_MAX`, and skip stale heap entries with `if (cur.first > dis[node]) continue;` to stay fast.

check.q: Why does following `par` from n give the path backwards?
check.a: Each node stores only who came right before it, so you walk from the end to the start and must reverse at the end.

files.title: Outsbook: Sundorbon (grid BFS)
files.what: Find the fewest moves from S to E on a square map where T cells are blocked. BFS from S fills `level` for every reachable cell; print `level` at E. Repeats until end of input.
steps: `while (cin >> n)`: read the grid character by character, remembering the S and E positions.
BFS from S (the function is named `dfs`, but it uses a queue, so it is BFS): push neighbours that are inside, not 'T', and unvisited, with `level = parent level + 1`.
files.complexity: Time O(n^2) per map · Space O(n^2)
files.input:
5
S P P P P
T P T P P
T P P P P
P T E T T
P T P T T
3
S P T
T P T
E P P
files.input_note: Maps one after another until EOF: n, then n rows of letters. The first map is the sample (expected 5).
files.output_note: `5` for the first map and `4` for the second (S right, down, down, left).
files.watch_out: The function name `dfs` is misleading: it is a BFS, and only BFS guarantees the fewest moves. Tip: on some compilers you need `#include <cstring>` for `memset`; this file relies on another header bringing it in.

check.q: Why would a DFS not give the minimum number of moves here?
check.a: DFS follows one path deep first and may reach E by a long route; BFS explores cells in order of distance, so the first time it reaches a cell is the shortest.

recap: DSU can keep component count and largest size updated after each union.
An edge inside one component is redundant and can be traded for a link between components.
Store `par[child]` in Dijkstra/BFS to print the path; walk back and reverse.
Unit-cost grid = BFS; the level of a cell is its minimum distance.
Never give a local variable the same name as a global array you still need.

check_yourself.q: 10 cities, no roads, then 4 roads that never create a cycle. How many components now?
check_yourself.a: 6. Each useful road reduces the count by one.

check_yourself.q: Which algorithm fits: 'fewest moves on a grid' vs 'cheapest route with different road costs'?
check_yourself.a: Fewest moves: BFS. Different costs: Dijkstra.

check_yourself.q: What value marks 'no parent' in the Dijkstra path code, and why is it needed?
check_yourself.a: -1. The walk back stops when it reaches -1, which happens just after the source node.
